chunks: 2697 - The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله passed by Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah al-Anṣārī while he was in ihram, and lice had consumed his head, his eyebrows, and his eyes. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “I did not think that the matter would reach what I see.”
Then he commanded him, so he offered a sacrificial rite on his behalf, and he shaved his head, by the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
"But whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head, then a ransom of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice."

So the fasting is three days, and the charity is for six needy persons, for each needy person a sāʿ of dates. And it has been narrated: “A mudd of dates, and the sacrificial rite is a sheep from which no one may eat except the needy.”

key_terms.الْقَمْلُ: lice that caused severe harm to the head
key_terms.صَدَقَةٍ: charity given to needy persons as expiation
key_terms.صِيَامٍ: fasting as one of the forms of fidyah
key_terms.فَفِدْيَةٌ: a compensatory expiation due for necessary violation in ihram
key_terms.مَسَاكِينُ: needy persons who are entitled to receive the charity or meat
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of ihram during hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.نُسُكٍ: sacrificial offering as a form of expiation

ai.seo_question: What is the fidyah for a person in ihram who shaves the head because of illness or harm?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for a muhrim who must shave due to harm affecting the head, such as severe lice infestation. It applies the Qur'anic verse on fidyah by specifying the available forms of expiation: fasting, charity, or sacrifice.
